description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic known for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered to perfection in a mildly spiced, fragrant gravy. This dish offers a harmonious blend of sweet, tangy, and savory flavors, making it a truly irresistible culinary experience.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts
Red chili powder or Kashmiri chili powder

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 min, then blended to a paste

ingredients.item: Heavy cream or half and half

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the cubed chicken with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover the bowl and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil or ghee in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, without overcrowding the pan, and sear until lightly browned on all sides. The chicken does not need to be fully cooked at this stage. Remove the seared chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Cashew Paste
instructions.text: If not already done, soak the cashews in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain and blend them with a minimal amount of fresh water to form a smooth, thick paste. Set aside.

instructions.title: Build the Makhani Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same skillet, melt 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes, ground cumin, ground coriander, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon of garam masala. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken and the oil to separate slightly.

instructions.title: Simmer the Chicken in Sauce
instructions.text: Add the seared chicken and the cashew paste to the tomato sauce. Stir well to combine. Add about 1/2 cup of water to adjust the consistency if the sauce is too thick. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until the chicken is cooked through and tender, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Remove the lid. Stir in the heavy cream or half and half, crushed Kasoori Methi dried fenugreek leaves, and honey or sugar. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter and let it melt into the sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and sugar if needed. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, ensuring the sauce is heated through but not boiled vigorously after adding cream.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Garnish the classic Butter Chicken with a drizzle of extra cream and fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with steamed basmati rice, naan bread, or roti for a complete and satisfying Indian meal.

tips: For an extra smoky flavor, char the seared chicken slightly under a broiler or on a grill before adding it to the sauce.
Do not skip the Kasoori Methi dried fenugreek leaves; they are crucial for the authentic flavor profile of Butter Chicken.
Butter Chicken tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
article:
The aroma of rich spices, tender chicken, and a velvety smooth, tomato-based sauce is synonymous with one of India's most beloved culinary creations: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian chicken recipe has transcended borders, captivating palates worldwide with its irresistible balance of sweet, savory, and subtly spicy notes. If you’ve ever yearned to recreate that restaurant-quality dish in your own kitchen, you’re in the right place. Join us as we delve into the heart of classic Murgh Makhani, exploring its origins, essential ingredients, and a step-by-step guide to mastering this creamy, dreamy delight. Prepare to impress your family and friends with a dish that’s truly a celebration of Indian flavors.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, translates literally to "chicken with butter" – a fitting name for a dish renowned for its rich, buttery, and creamy texture. Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant, it was reportedly created by Kundan Lal Gujral. The story goes that leftover tandoori chicken pieces were simmered in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream, giving birth to a legend.

At its core, Butter Chicken features succulent pieces of marinated and often char-grilled chicken swimming in a luxurious, vibrant orange or red sauce. This sauce is a complex symphony of pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and a medley of aromatic spices like garam masala, cumin, and coriander. What truly sets Murgh Makhani apart is the generous use of butter (makhan) and fresh cream, which lend it an unparalleled richness and a slightly sweet, tangy finish. Unlike some other Indian curries that can be intensely spicy, classic Butter Chicken is typically mild, focusing instead on depth of flavor and a comforting mouthfeel, making it a universal crowd-pleaser among Indian chicken recipes.

## Ingredients for Classic Butter Chicken

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken requires a careful selection of ingredients, each playing a vital role in building its signature flavor profile. Don't be intimidated by the list; many are pantry staples in Indian cooking.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   **Boneless, Skinless Chicken:** Thighs are preferred for their juiciness, cut into 1-inch pieces.
*   **Plain Yogurt:** Tenderizes the chicken and helps spices adhere.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** The aromatic foundation.
*   **Spices:** Red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color without excessive heat), turmeric powder, garam masala, salt.
*   **Lemon Juice:** Adds a touch of acidity and brightness.

**For the Silky Makhani Sauce:**
*   **Butter:** A generous amount is crucial for flavor and richness.
*   **Onions:** Finely chopped, forms part of the gravy base.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** More aromatics for the sauce.
*   **Canned Crushed Tomatoes or Fresh Tomato Puree:** The backbone of the sauce, providing tang and body.
*   **Cashews (or Blanched Almonds):** Soaked, then blended, they create incredible creaminess and thickness.
*   **Heavy Cream:** The defining ingredient for that luxurious, velvety texture.
*   **Spices:** Kashmiri red chili powder (again, for color), turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala.
*   **Kasoori Methi (Dried Fenugreek Leaves):** A non-negotiable ingredient, providing a unique, slightly bitter, savory aroma.
*   **Sugar:** A pinch balances the acidity of the tomatoes.
*   **Salt:** To taste.
*   **Water or Chicken Broth:** To adjust sauce consistency.

**For Garnish:**
*   Fresh Coriander (Cilantro): Chopped, for freshness.
*   A Swirl of Heavy Cream: For presentation and an extra touch of decadence.

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Butter Chicken

While the ingredient list might seem extensive, making Butter Chicken is a straightforward process that yields incredibly rewarding results.

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor and tenderness.

**Step 2: Cook the Chicken**
Heat a little oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until the chicken is lightly charred on the outside and mostly cooked through. You can also grill or bake the chicken for a more authentic tandoori flavor. Set the cooked chicken aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Sauce Base**
In the same pan (or a separate large pot), melt a generous amount of butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until translucent. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews, Kashmiri chili powder, turmeric, cumin, and coriander powder. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes until the tomatoes soften and the mixture thickens slightly, and the oil starts to separate.

**Step 4: Blend the Sauce**
Remove the sauce base from heat and let it cool slightly. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until absolutely smooth. For an extra silky sauce, you can strain the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot, pressing down on the solids to extract all the liquid.

**Step 5: Finish the Sauce**
Return the smooth sauce to the pot over medium-low heat. Add the garam masala, kasoori methi (crushed between your palms to release its aroma), sugar, and salt to taste. Stir well. Pour in the heavy cream and simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken to your desired consistency.

**Step 6: Combine and Serve**
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering sauce. Stir gently to coat the chicken completely. Let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes to allow the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Garnish generously with fresh chopped coriander and a final swirl of cream before serving your exquisite Butter Chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that perfect restaurant-quality Butter Chicken is within reach with a few expert tricks:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marinating time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is best!
*   **Char the Chicken:** If possible, lightly charring the chicken (whether pan-frying, grilling, or baking at high heat) before adding it to the sauce adds a depth of smoky flavor that elevates the dish.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** For the ultimate smooth sauce, ensure you blend the tomato-cashew mixture thoroughly. Straining it afterwards is an optional but highly recommended step for a truly luxurious texture.
*   **Toast Kasoori Methi:** Lightly toast the kasoori methi in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing it between your palms. This intensifies its unique aroma and flavor.
*   **Balance the Flavors:** Taste your sauce frequently. The balance between sweet (sugar), tangy (tomatoes), and rich (cream/butter) is crucial. Adjust salt, sugar, and even a touch more lemon juice if needed.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Using fresh, high-quality spices, good butter, and heavy cream will make a noticeable difference in the final taste of your Murgh Makhani.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Butter Chicken is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when paired with traditional Indian accompaniments.

*   **Breads:** The classic choice is warm, fluffy Naan bread (plain, garlic, or butter naan) for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce. Tandoori roti or flaky parathas are also excellent choices.
*   **Rice:** Steamed Basmati rice or fragrant Jeera (cumin) rice provides a perfect contrast and absorbs the creamy gravy beautifully.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber or mint raita (yogurt dip) helps to balance the richness of the curry.
*   **Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice) adds a refreshing crunch.
*   **Beverages:** A sweet or salty Lassi (yogurt drink) is a classic pairing. For alcoholic options, a light Indian lager or a crisp white wine like a Sauvignon Blanc can complement the flavors without overpowering them.

## Variations and FAQs

**Variations:**
*   **Healthier Butter Chicken:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, substituting some of the cream with Greek yogurt (added at the end to prevent curdling) or even a splash of milk.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For an authentic restaurant-style smoky flavor, try the "Dhungaar" method. Place a small, heat-proof bowl in the finished curry, place a hot charcoal briquette in it, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over the charcoal, and quickly cover the pot for a few minutes.
*   **Vegetarian Butter Paneer:** Replace the chicken with cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese), which can be lightly fried or grilled before adding to the sauce.
*   **Vegan Butter Chicken:** Use plant-based butter, coconut cream instead of heavy cream, and marinated tofu or chickpeas instead of chicken.

**FAQs:**

**Q: Can I make Butter Chicken ahead of time?**
A: Absolutely! Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.

**Q: Can I freeze Butter Chicken?**
A: Yes, it freezes well. Allow it to cool completely, then transfer to freezer-safe containers. It can be frozen for up to 2-3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water or cream if needed to adjust consistency.

**Q: Is Butter Chicken supposed to be spicy?**
A: Classic Butter Chicken is generally mild with a subtle warmth. The primary spice, Kashmiri red chili powder, is used more for its vibrant red color than intense heat. You can adjust the heat level by adding more or less regular red chili powder to your preference.

**Q: What's the difference between Butter Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala?**
A: While both are creamy, tomato-based chicken curries, Butter Chicken is typically richer, sweeter, and milder, with a more pronounced buttery and creamy flavor. Chicken Tikka Masala often has a stronger spice profile, a slightly tangier taste, and less emphasis on butter and cream, though it still has a creamy base. The chicken in Tikka Masala is almost always chargrilled Tikka (marinated in yogurt and spices), whereas Butter Chicken can use pan-fried or baked chicken.

Mastering Butter Chicken is a culinary journey that promises delicious rewards. With this comprehensive guide, you’re well-equipped to create a classic Murgh Makhani that will transport your taste buds straight to the heart of India. Enjoy the process, savor the flavors, and delight in one of the world's most cherished Indian chicken recipes.
